tiers.title: Meet the board
tiers.goal: Your child can name every square and move every piece legally.

tiers.title: Playing a real game
tiers.goal: Your child can play a full legal game start to finish, including castling and checkmate.

tiers.title: Don't give it away
tiers.goal: Your child stops hanging pieces and starts counting what a trade is worth.

tiers.title: Tricks and traps
tiers.goal: Your child can spot forks, pins, and skewers in a real position.

tiers.title: Finishing the game
tiers.goal: Your child can deliver checkmate on purpose instead of by accident.

tiers.title: The last few pieces
tiers.goal: Your child knows what to do when almost everything is gone.

tiers.title: Play and improve
tiers.goal: Your child plays rated games and reviews their own mistakes with the coach.

units.title: Every square has a colour
units.concept: The board alternates light and dark, and the bottom-right square is always light.

script.say: This is a chessboard. Sixty-four squares.
Half of them are light. Half are dark.
The square in the bottom right corner is always light. Always. Remember that one.

voiceover.intro: Let's look at the board before we touch any pieces.
voiceover.success: That's it. Light on the right.
voiceover.hintTier1: Look at the corner nearest your hand.
voiceover.retry: Not that one. Try the other corner.

units.title: Squares have names
units.concept: Columns are letters a to h, rows are numbers 1 to 8, and every square has one name like e4.

script.say: Columns go up and down. They have letters.
Rows go side to side. They have numbers.
Where they cross is e4. Letter first, then number.

voiceover.intro: Every square has a name. Once you know them, you can talk about chess with anyone in the world.
voiceover.hintTier1: Find the letter along the bottom first.
voiceover.hintTier2: Now slide your finger up to the number.

units.title: The rook goes straight
units.concept: The rook moves any number of squares along a row or column, but never diagonally.

voiceover.intro: The rook is the castle tower. It only likes straight lines.
voiceover.hintTier1: Rooks can't go diagonally. Try along the row or the column.
voiceover.retry: That's a diagonal. The rook can't do that one.

units.title: The bishop stays on its colour
units.concept: The bishop moves diagonally, which means it can never leave the colour it started on.

voiceover.intro: The bishop only moves on slants. Watch what that means.
voiceover.hintTier1: Look at the colour your bishop is standing on. It can only reach that colour.
voiceover.retry: That square is the wrong colour for this bishop.

units.title: The queen does both
units.concept: The queen moves like a rook and a bishop combined.

voiceover.intro: You already know the queen. She's a rook and a bishop in one.
voiceover.hintTier1: Straight lines or slants. Both work.

units.title: The knight hops
units.concept: The knight moves in an L and jumps over anything in the way.

voiceover.intro: The knight is the strange one. It jumps.
voiceover.hintTier1: Two squares one way, then one square to the side.
voiceover.hintTier2: The knight always lands on the opposite colour to where it started.

units.title: The king takes one step
units.concept: The king moves one square in any direction.

voiceover.intro: The king is slow. One step at a time, any direction.

units.title: The pawn only goes forward
units.concept: The pawn moves forward one square but captures diagonally, and it can never go back.

voiceover.intro: The pawn is the only piece that moves one way and captures another way.
voiceover.success: Forward to move, slanted to capture.
voiceover.hintTier1: To take a piece, the pawn goes diagonally. Straight ahead is only for moving.

units.title: Taking a piece
units.concept: You capture by landing on an enemy piece, and it leaves the board.

voiceover.intro: Now the fun part. Taking pieces.

units.title: A pawn can become a queen
units.concept: A pawn that reaches the far side turns into any piece you choose, usually a queen.

voiceover.intro: Every pawn dreams of getting to the other side.

units.title: The king is in trouble
units.concept: Check means the king is attacked and you must deal with it immediately.

units.title: Three ways out of check
units.concept: Move the king, block the attacker, or capture the attacker.

units.title: No way out
units.concept: Checkmate is check with none of the three escapes available. That ends the game.

units.title: Nobody wins
units.concept: Stalemate is no legal move and no check, and the game is a draw.

units.title: The king hides
units.concept: Castling moves the king two squares toward a rook and jumps the rook over it, if neither has moved.

units.title: Your first whole game
units.concept: Everything so far, played end to end against a very gentle opponent.

units.title: What each piece is worth
units.concept: Pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. The king is priceless.

units.title: Is it defended?
units.concept: A piece nobody is defending can be taken for free. Check before you move.

units.title: Good trade or bad trade
units.concept: Count attackers and defenders before you capture.

units.title: How to start
units.concept: Take the centre, bring out knights and bishops, castle early, and leave the queen home at first.

units.title: The knight forks
units.concept: One knight attacking two pieces at once. They can't both run.

units.title: Stuck in place
units.concept: A pinned piece can't move because something more valuable is behind it.

units.title: The pin backwards
units.concept: The valuable piece is in front, so when it moves you take what was behind it.

units.title: Move one, attack with another
units.concept: Moving a piece out of the way opens an attack from the piece behind it.

units.title: Two rooks walk the king
units.concept: Two rooks cut the king off row by row until it runs out of board.

units.title: Trapped behind its own pawns
units.concept: A king with pawns in front of it and no escape square dies on the back rank.

units.title: King and queen finish it
units.concept: Push the enemy king to the edge with the queen, then bring your own king up.

units.title: Two moves ahead
units.concept: Force the answer you want, then finish.

units.title: Can the king catch it?
units.concept: Draw a square from the pawn to the promotion rank. If the king can step inside, it catches the pawn.

units.title: Kings face off
units.concept: The king that does not have to move first wins the standoff.

units.title: Play for real
units.concept: Rated games against bots matched to your level.

units.title: What went wrong
units.concept: The coach walks through your own game and shows the moment it turned.
